items.description:
Indonesian police recovered seven body bags and rescuers were searching for about 50 workers who were missing on Sunday after a fire tore through a factory in western Java, as firefighters tackled hotspots over a day after the blaze broke out.
One body bag might contain body parts from several people, police said.
Authorities said the intensity of the fire had rendered the recovered victims unidentifiable via visual inspection, prompting efforts to collect DNA samples from relatives and personal belongings of the missing workers.

items.title: Veteran journalist Husain Naqi passes away in Lahore
items.description:
LAHORE: Veteran journalist and human rights activist Husain Naqi passed away in Lahore on Sunday of a cardiac arrest.
He was a former editor of The News and had also been associated with the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP).
On Saturday, a day before his passing, Naqi attended a book launch organised by HRCP. Later in the day, at 6pm, he suffered a cardiac attack, after which he was admitted at a private hospital, according to HRCP official Muhammad Ilyas.
Naqi passed away on Sunday morning at 5am. He left behind three sons.
President Asif Ali Zardari extended his condolences on Naqi

items.description:
Lahore topped the list of the world’s most polluted major cities once again on Sunday morning with an hourly air quality index (AQI) reading of over 500, according to real-time air quality data.

items.title: Textile exports rise 6.35pc in July-October
items.description:

items.title: Journalist’s bail plea rejected
items.description:
QUETTA: A local court in Quetta on Saturday rejected the bail application of Islamabad-based journalist Shahid Maitla.
The bail application was filed by Rahib Buledi Advocate and other lawyers in the court of Judicial Magistrate-VII.
Judicial Magistrate Akhtar Shah, who had reserved the verdict on the application, announced the decision.
Shahid Maitla was arrested under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act (Peca) on a complaint lodged by former caretaker prime minister Anwarul Haq Kakar. After his arrest, Shahid Maitla was shifted from Islamabad to Quetta.He is currently on judicial remand

items.title: Security forces kill 15 terrorists in Balochistan's Mastung district: state media
items.description:
Security forces have killed 15 terrorists during two separate operations in Balochistan’s Mastung district, state media reported on Saturday.
According to security sources cited by Radio Pakistan, five terrorists were killed in the first operation, while 10 others were eliminated in the second one. Both were conducted against Fitna al Hindustan under ‘Operation Raddul Fitna 3’, which began in August.
The state has designated outlawed Balochistan-based groups as Fitna al Hindustan to highlight India’s role in terrorism and destabilisation across Pakistan.
